classes.definition: warrant that is listed on a securities exchange

classes.name: exotic warrant
classes.label: exotic warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right (but not the obligation) to buy (or sometimes sell) an underlying asset under non-standard or complex conditions, often involving additional features not found in a plain vanilla (standard) warrant

classes.name: index warrant
classes.label: index warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount based on the performance of an index during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: long mini-future certificate
classes.label: long mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that typically entitles the holder to acquire specific underlying assets during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: mini-future certificate
classes.label: mini-future certificate
classes.definition: entitlement that combines the structure of an open-end certificate with a leverage option with no fixed term, making leverage available without a term restriction, and whose payoff depends on whether or not the underlying asset has reached or exceeded a predetermined price

classes.name: naked warrant
classes.label: naked warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued without an accompanying security by a third party that does not hold as many securities as would be required if all the warrants are exercised

classes.name: perpetual warrant
classes.label: perpetual warrant
classes.definition: warrant without an expiration date, giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a certain strike price

classes.name: preferred convertible share purchase right
classes.label: preferred convertible share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred, convertible shareholders the right to buy preferred, convertible shares of the firm or preferred, convertible shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: preferred convertible share subscription right
classes.label: preferred convertible share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred, convertible shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: preferred share purchase right
classes.label: preferred share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred shareholders the right to buy preferred shares of the firm or preferred shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: preferred share subscription right
classes.label: preferred share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: private warrant
classes.label: private warrant
classes.definition: warrant that is not tradable

classes.name: public warrant
classes.label: public warrant
classes.definition: warrant that may be traded over the counter (OTC) or through an exchange

classes.name: purchase right
classes.label: purchase right
classes.definition: anti-takeover device that gives a prospective acquiree's shareholders the right to buy shares of the firm or shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: put warrant
classes.label: put warrant
classes.definition: warrant giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified (i.e., acquire cash in exchange for the underlying assets, such as stock) back to the issuer at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

classes.name: short mini-future certificate
classes.label: short mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that entitles the holder to acquire cash in exchange for specific underlying assets

classes.name: structured warrant
classes.label: structured warrant
classes.definition: warrant that is listed on an exchange, offering investors a way to participate in the price performance of an underlying asset without buying it directly

classes.name: subscription right
classes.label: subscription right
classes.definition: privileges allotted to existing security holders, entitling them to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: traditional warrant
classes.label: traditional warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued by the issuer of the underlying instrument

classes.name: warrant
classes.label: warrant
classes.definition: entitlement that permits the holder to purchase a specified amount of a financial instrument, commodity, currency or other asset during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: barrier capital protection certificate
classes.label: barrier capital protection certificate
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: barrier discount certificate
classes.label: barrier discount certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the maximum redemption amount (Cap) is paid out if the barrier is never breached

classes.name: barrier reverse convertible certificate
classes.label: barrier reverse convertible certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the barrier never be breached, the nominal price plus coupon is paid at redemption; if the barrier is breached the product changes into a reverse convertible

classes.name: basket certificate
classes.label: basket certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose underlying asset represents a fraction of a basket of securities that corresponds to the subscription ratio

classes.name: bonus certificate
classes.label: bonus certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with a greater risk in relation to multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of), allowing for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and with a reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: capital-protected product
classes.label: capital-protected product
classes.definition: structured product that participates in the performance of a financial asset, such as a stock, fund or index, while protecting the investor's capital

classes.name: capital protection certificate with coupons
classes.label: capital protection certificate with coupons
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: capital protection certificate with participation
classes.label: capital protection certificate with participation
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal amount (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: capital protection convertible certificate
classes.label: capital protection convertible certificate
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: discount certificate
classes.label: discount certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the underlying asset(s) and/or a cash amount is redeemed should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, for which, in return, the potential profit is capped

classes.name: express certificate
classes.label: express certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying trade above the strike on the observation date, an early redemption consisting of nominal price plus an additional coupon amount is paid

classes.name: index certificate
classes.label: index certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose underlying asset is an index

classes.name: leveraged product
classes.label: leveraged product
classes.definition: structured product that provides a further enhanced yield (over and above that of a yield-enhancement product), often without any limit to the upside participation, and frequently with a stop-loss in order to limit potential capital losses

classes.name: outperformance bonus certificate
classes.label: outperformance bonus certificate
classes.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, in which the minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with greater risk multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of) allow for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: outperformance certificate
classes.label: outperformance certificate
classes.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, reflecting underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees), and whose risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: participation certificate
classes.label: participation certificate
classes.definition: participation product that provides the possibility to participate in the gains or losses in the price of an asset, subject to counterparty risk

classes.name: participation instrument
classes.label: participation instrument
classes.definition: structured product that provides the possibility to participate in the performance of an asset or basket of assets

classes.name: reverse convertible certificate
classes.label: reverse convertible certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, the underlying asset(s) and/ or a cash amount is redeemed; should the underlying asset close above the strike at expiry, the nominal amount plus the coupon is paid at redemption

classes.name: structured product
classes.label: structured product
classes.definition: security whose cash flow characteristics depend upon one or more indices or that have embedded forwards or options or securities where an investor's investment return and the issuer's payment obligations are contingent on, or highly sensitive to, changes in the value of underlying assets, indices, interest rates or cash flows

classes.name: tracker certificate
classes.label: tracker certificate
classes.definition: certificate that reflects underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by conversion ratio and any related fees), in which the associated risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: turbo certificate
classes.label: turbo certificate
classes.definition: certificate that acts as a leveraged security, whose price tracks an underlying financial asset's price one for one, and that can be used to go long or short

classes.name: twin-win certificate
classes.label: twin-win certificate
classes.definition: certificate that makes profits possible with rising and falling underlying asset values, in which a falling underlying asset price converts into profit up to the barrier, and whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached

classes.name: yield-enhancement product
classes.label: yield-enhancement product
classes.definition: structured product that provides a predefined yield in return for a downside risk

classes.name: basis swap
classes.label: basis swap
classes.definition: swap in which payment streams are referenced to different bases

classes.name: correlation leg
classes.label: correlation leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a correlation swap that pays an amount based on the observed average correlation of the prices of a collection of underlying products

classes.name: correlation swap
classes.label: correlation swap
classes.definition: over-the-counter statistical derivative that allows one to hedge risks associated with the observed average correlation of a collection of underlying products

classes.name: dispersion leg
classes.label: dispersion leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a dispersion swap that pays an amount based on the realized dispersion of the price changes of the underlying product

classes.name: dispersion swap
classes.label: dispersion swap
classes.definition: statistical derivative used to hedge on the magnitude of a price movement of an underlying asset

classes.name: excess return swap
classes.label: excess return swap
classes.definition: return swap in which the change in the level of the index will be equal to the returns generated primarily by the changes in price of each of the contracts that comprise the index

classes.name: fixed leg
classes.label: fixed leg
classes.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate or consisting of at least one payment of a fixed amount

classes.name: fixed payment leg
classes.label: fixed payment leg
classes.definition: swap leg that specifies contractual terms associated with a schedule of payments for any swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate

classes.name: floating leg
classes.label: floating leg
classes.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to some variable rate, calculated based on the change in value of some underlying asset, or consisting of at least one payment of some floating amount

classes.name: index return swap
classes.label: index return swap
classes.definition: return swap in which payments are based on a fee paid to the seller of the swap and on a floating reference price based on changes in the level of an index from an initial level to a level observed on some valuation date(s)

classes.name: major swap participant
classes.label: major swap participant
classes.definition: financial service provider that maintains a substantial position in swaps for any of the major swap categories

classes.name: performance-based variable leg
classes.label: performance-based variable leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

classes.name: rate-based leg
classes.label: rate-based leg
classes.definition: swap leg of a rate-based swap based on a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

classes.name: rates swap
classes.label: rates swap
classes.definition: swap in two counterparties each agree to pay the other cash flows on defined dates during an agreed period, based on a specified notional amount and a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

classes.name: realized variable leg
classes.label: realized variable leg
classes.definition: performance-based leg wherein the payment is netted at maturity rather than periodically

classes.name: return leg
classes.label: return leg
classes.definition: leg of a swap in which the income generated by some underlier is paid

classes.name: return swap
classes.label: return swap
classes.definition: swap in which one leg, the return leg, is based on income generated from some underlier

classes.name: simple return leg
classes.label: simple return leg
classes.definition: return leg based strictly on the income generated by the underlying asset, excluding appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

classes.name: statistical swap
classes.label: statistical swap
classes.definition: swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

classes.name: strike leg
classes.label: strike leg
classes.definition: swap leg that specifies a fixed amount, 'the strike', quoted at the time of execution

classes.name: swap
classes.label: swap
classes.definition: derivative instrument whereby counterparties agree to exchange periodic streams of cash flows or liabilities from two different financial instruments with each other

classes.name: swap confirmation
classes.label: swap confirmation
classes.definition: formal confirmation that codifies the terms and conditions specific to a lifecycle event with respect to the overall transaction between the parties

classes.name: swap data repository
classes.label: swap data repository
classes.definition: financial service provider that provides a central facility for swap data reporting and recordkeeping

classes.name: swap dealer
classes.label: swap dealer
classes.definition: non-depository institution such as one that deals in swaps, makes a market in swaps, regularly enters into swaps with counterparties as an ordinary course of business for its own account, and engages in any activity causing the person to be commonly known in the trade as a dealer/market maker in swaps

classes.name: swap leg
classes.label: swap leg
classes.definition: terms defining and the commitment to fulfill cashflow requirements (e.g., interest payments, coupon payments, etc.) for a component of a swap

classes.name: swap leg event
classes.label: swap leg event
classes.definition: swap lifecycle event, such as a payment or rate reset event, that applies to one leg of a swap

classes.name: swap lifecycle event
classes.label: swap lifecycle event
classes.definition: event that occurs during the lifecycle of a swap, where the overall set of events includes those specific to the issuer, front office, middle office, and/or back office processes

classes.name: swap lifecycle event identifier
classes.label: swap lifecycle event identifier
classes.definition: identifier that uniquely identifies a specific event in the lifecycle of a swap

classes.name: swap party
classes.label: swap party
classes.definition: party to a swap and therefore a legal party to the contract that embodies that transaction

classes.name: swap paying party
classes.label: swap paying party
classes.definition: swap party responsible for making payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

classes.name: swap receiving party
classes.label: swap receiving party
classes.definition: swap party that receives payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

classes.name: swap terms
classes.label: swap terms
classes.definition: legal contractual terms of a swap transaction

classes.name: total return leg
classes.label: total return leg
classes.definition: return leg based on the income generated by the underlying asset as well as any appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

classes.name: total return swap
classes.label: total return swap
classes.definition: return swap where the seller agrees to pay the other party the difference in value of some underlying asset multiplied by an agreed-upon notional value should the asset value increase between specified periods of time

classes.name: unique swap identifier
classes.label: unique swap identifier
classes.definition: identifier for a swap that is used in recordkeeping and swap data reporting

edges.name: has commodity value as of date
edges.label: has commodity value as of date
edges.definition: indicates the per unit value of a given commodity as of some specified date

edges.name: has grade
edges.label: has grade
edges.definition: The grade of oil e.g. Brent Crude.

edges.name: has forward exchange rate
edges.label: has forward exchange rate
edges.definition: rate of exchange between two currencies as specified in a forward contract

edges.name: has spot exchange rate
edges.label: has spot exchange rate
edges.definition: rate of exchange between two currencies as specified as of some date and time as quoted by a specific source, typically for a spot contract

edges.name: has accreting notional amount
edges.label: has accreting notional amount
edges.definition: indicates that the notional amount increases through the life of the contract

edges.name: has additional costs
edges.label: has additional costs
edges.definition: indicates costs, such as up front costs, brokerage fees and the like, that must be paid on delivery

edges.name: has amortizing notional amount
edges.label: has amortizing notional amount
edges.definition: indicates that the notional amount decreases through the life of the contract

edges.name: has constant notional amount
edges.label: has constant notional amount
edges.definition: indicates that the notional amount is constant through the life of the contract

edges.name: has custom notional amount
edges.label: has custom notional amount
edges.definition: indicates that the notional amount is customized per a notional step schedule

edges.name: has first delivery date
edges.label: has first delivery date
edges.definition: specifies the initial date in a range of dates by which the underlying asset (or some portion thereof) must be delivered in order for the terms of the contract to be fulfilled

edges.name: has first notice date
edges.label: has first notice date
edges.definition: specifies the initial date on which a delivery notice can be issued

edges.name: has last delivery date
edges.label: has last delivery date
edges.definition: specifies the final date in a range of dates by which the underlying asset (or some portion thereof) must be delivered in order for the terms of the contract to be fulfilled

edges.name: has last notice date
edges.label: has last notice date
edges.definition: specifies the final date on which a delivery notice can be issued

edges.name: has settlement terms
edges.label: has settlement terms
edges.definition: relates a derivative to contractual terms specific to the settlement process

edges.name: has tick value
edges.label: has tick value
edges.definition: indicates the cash value of one tick, i.e., the minimum price change of the contract

edges.name: has underlying asset price
edges.label: has underlying asset price
edges.definition: specifies a price for something on which the contract is based

edges.name: has valuation terms
edges.label: has valuation terms
edges.definition: relates a derivative to contractual terms specific to valuation of the underlying asset(s)

edges.name: specifies value of
edges.label: specifies value of
edges.definition: relates a derivative to contractual terms specific to valuation of the underlying asset(s)

edges.name: has Asian tail period
edges.label: has Asian tail period
edges.definition: window of time during which averaging of the price of the underlying contract is effective

edges.name: has first barrier price
edges.label: has first barrier price
edges.definition: has price (or level) that activates or deactivates the option

edges.name: has first rebate amount
edges.label: has first rebate amount
edges.definition: indicates the percentage of the premium paid by the holder for the option

edges.name: has lookback period
edges.label: has lookback period
edges.definition: window of time during which the lookback is effective

edges.name: has monitoring period
edges.label: has monitoring period
edges.definition: window of time during which pricing is monitored

edges.name: has option type election date
edges.label: has option type election date
edges.definition: indicates the date on which the holder of the chooser option contract determines a choice of either a call or a put

edges.name: has second barrier price
edges.label: has second barrier price
edges.definition: has price (or level) that the second barrier activates or deactivates in the case of a double barrier option

edges.name: has second rebate amount
edges.label: has second rebate amount
edges.definition: indicates the percentage of the premium paid by the holder in the case of a double barrier option

edges.name: uses currency in averaging
edges.label: uses currency in averaging
edges.definition: indicates the currency used in averaging calculation

edges.name: has dividend adjustment period
edges.label: has dividend adjustment period
edges.definition: indicates at least one date period used to calculate the deviation between an anticipated/expected dividend and the actual dividend issued during that period

edges.name: has method of adjustment
edges.label: has method of adjustment
edges.definition: indicates the method used to address any changes to the contract based on events that occur over the contract lifecycle

edges.name: has calculated market value
edges.label: has calculated market value
edges.definition: indicates a calculated price as of some relative date considered the market value of the option at that point in time

edges.name: has cap price
edges.label: has cap price
edges.definition: price at which the contract may be exercised

edges.name: has exercise date offset
edges.label: has exercise date offset
edges.definition: indicates the period in days between the reset date and the exercise date

edges.name: has exercise price
edges.label: has exercise price
edges.definition: specifies a predetermined price at which the holder commits to buy or sell an underlying asset

edges.name: has exercise schedule
edges.label: has exercise schedule
edges.definition: links an option to the schedule specified in the contract that constrains when it may be exercised

edges.name: has exercise style
edges.label: has exercise style
edges.definition: indicates the exercise convention specified for the option

edges.name: has interest accrual date offset
edges.label: has interest accrual date offset
edges.definition: indicates the period in days between each reset date and the commencement of interest accrual for the next period

edges.name: has option holder
edges.label: has option holder
edges.definition: indicates the owner of the option

edges.name: has option writer
edges.label: has option writer
edges.definition: indicates the issuer of the option

edges.name: has settlement date offset
edges.label: has settlement date offset
edges.definition: indicats the period in days between each reset date and the corresponding settlement date

edges.name: has strike percentage amount
edges.label: has strike percentage amount
edges.definition: indicates a strike price or level expressed as a percentage of the value of the underlying asset

edges.name: has strike rate
edges.label: has strike rate
edges.definition: rate at which the contract may be exercised

edges.name: has funding leg
edges.label: has funding leg
edges.definition: indicates the leg of a return swap that specifies a set payment rate, typically benchmark based but possibly a fixed rate

edges.name: has leg
edges.label: has leg
edges.definition: relates a swap contract to a leg that is part of that swap

edges.name: has return leg
edges.label: has return leg
edges.definition: indicates the leg of a return swap whose payments are based on the return of an underlying asset

edges.name: has swap identifier
edges.label: has swap identifier
edges.definition: relates a swap lifecycle event to the identifier for the swap

edges.name: is leg of
edges.label: is leg of
edges.definition: relates a swap leg to the to the swap that includes it

attributes.name: has monitoring frequency
attributes.label: has monitoring frequency
attributes.definition: has frequency with respect to how often, in days, the asset price is checked to see if the barrier has been breached

attributes.name: is above strike price
attributes.label: is above strike price
attributes.definition: indicates whether the barrier is crossed when the price of the underlier is above (or below, if not) the strike price (threshold)

attributes.name: uses weighted average
attributes.label: uses weighted average
attributes.definition: indicates whether a weighted average is being used to calculate the average rate or strike price

attributes.name: has conversion factor
attributes.label: has conversion factor
attributes.definition: indicates the price of the delivered bond/note ($1 par value) to yield a fixed rate. The conversion factor is used to calculate a final delivery price.

attributes.name: has multiple
attributes.label: has multiple
attributes.definition: indicates the multiple for determining the price of the futures contract in relation to the underlying index rate

attributes.name: has conversion ratio
attributes.label: has conversion ratio
attributes.definition: indicates the factor used to determine the number of warrants needed in order to buy or sell a specific number of securities or investment units

attributes.name: has oversubscribe option
attributes.label: has oversubscribe option
attributes.definition: indicates whether the holders of the rights instrument may get securities in the event that other right holders choose not to subscribe
